EXPEDITION REPORT

YOU FOUND THE LIGHT

GAME DESIGN BIBLE / PROTOTYPE V7

Survival is a problem
of architecture.

A systems-first pitch for a first-person 3D horror game. This playable vertical slice proves the core loop: digging changes navigation, supports control risk, cave-ins reshape pursuit, and scarce supplies turn each shortcut into a calculated gamble.

01 / EXPLOREFIND A SIGNAL

Traverse winding old workings. Fresh air enters from the surface lift, following connected tunnels and generally blowing deeper into the mine. The flame flickers downwind: move against the steady draft to find daylight. The airflow shifts after collapses and sometimes briefly reverses. A discovered-only chalk map shows where you've been.

02 / EXCAVATESHAPE THE LEVEL

Hold left mouse to excavate a rock face. Virgin rock costs 1 pick charge; clearing a cave-in costs 2. New passages stay vulnerable until protected.

03 / BRACEBUILD YOUR LIFELINE

Spend 1 timber to install a support at your feet. It stabilizes its own cell and neighboring cells. Unsupported fresh tunnels progressively deteriorate and eventually collapse.

04 / LISTENTHE MONSTER FINDS YOU

Three creatures gradually arrive. The Stalker tracks movement and breathes at close range, the Skitter rattles along the old tramway toward noise, and the pale Mourner sings when it sees candlelight. None can be defeated by fighting.

05 / SEALTURN SAFETY INTO A WEAPON

Aim at a beam in an adjacent supported tunnel and press Q. Its roof caves in instantly. The new blockage can buy time, but could sever the only safe route back.

06 / ESCAPEMAKE IT TO THE LIFT

Sprint briefly to open distance. Recharge by slowing down. Salvage amber caches to restore wax, pick strikes and timber. Follow the airflow through the forgotten workings to reach the lift, then ascend into daylight to win.

Current playable rules / V6

SystemRuleDesign consequence
MiningHold LMB ≈ 1 second; costs 1 charge. Rubble ≈ 1.7 seconds / 2 charges.Shortcuts are useful, but never free.
Roof stabilityNew tunnels begin with 36 integrity. Unsupported roofs decay over time; nearby timber prevents decay.Supports must be placed periodically in mined branches.
CollapseBreaking a targeted beam blocks its passage immediately. Natural instability can do the same.A one-way escape is powerful—and dangerous.
Digging resourcesStart with 9 pick strikes, cap 14; timber starts at 5, cap 9.Over-mining can leave you unable to recover.
SalvageAmber caches restore +3 charges, +1 timber, +21 wax.Exploration creates short-term survival rewards.
Sprint5.35 m/s, 29 stamina/second; walk 2.76 m/s, stamina restores 15.5/second.Running is an emergency maneuver, not a default speed.
CandleWax drains 0.44/second when lit; C extinguishes it. Flame physically leans with ventilation; surface air usually blows downhill away from the exit. Airflow changes with tunnel connectivity and occasional pressure reversals.Stealth, visibility and wayfinding all share one resource.
StalkerAppears after a warning; pursues along passable cells. Block its route and it searches for a new approach after a delay.Re-routing the creature, not killing it, is your defense.

Design pillars

1. Geometry is strategy: the level is a live defensive system. 2. Meaningful scarcity: wood, stamina, wax and pick strikes create competing priorities. 3. Fair fear: a warning precedes encounters; attacks follow traversable routes; escape is always possible with planning and supplies. 4. Readable danger: structural states, roof warnings, sound and light communicate risk. 5. No combat: fear comes from movement, preparation and topology.

This V6 prototype opens with a scripted cave-floor collapse, includes three unique monster silhouettes and controller support, and ends with a pressured hoist-cranking finale and a daylight escape sequence. It is made with native WebGL. It uses procedurally generated 3D geometry, deterministic mine generation, a grid-based chase AI, and 62 real CC0 recorded horror & mine foley audio stems. Future production work: a detailed photoreal mine kit, spatial audio and monster animations, authored event sequences, multi-stage objectives, difficulty modes, persistent map and accessibility options.
FIELD NOTES / 1891

Know your hands.

Hold F / LT while still: the flame points along a connected tunnel toward the lift. You have one TNT and no portable timber. Fresh excavations can collapse. Listen for breathing before you move.

WASDMove aroundMouse to look · left stick on controller
HOLD LMBDig the rock aheadRT on controller · uses pick strikes
E / AHide inside a cart / wind the liftTap near an abandoned ore cart to hide; hold at the hoist to escape
LMB / RTBreak a visible timberAny timber you break collapses its gallery
R / RBPlant rare TNT on rockRetreat before the fuse burns down
SHIFT / LBRun for your lifeUses stamina · you cannot run indefinitely
F / LTStand still and listenReveals the next reachable tunnel toward the exit; you cannot move
C / BCover / uncover the candleWax burns as you explore · F / LT bends the flame toward the exit

M = discovered map · H = controls · ESC = pause · Gamepad: LS move / RS look.
